record.paper_title: Recent Results and Open Problems in Evolutionary Multiobjective Optimization
record.original_question: How can multi-objective evolutionary algorithms explicitly handle constraints in constrained multi-objective optimization problems, beyond simple changes to Pareto dominance rules, and what benchmark problems should be used to evaluate constraint handling fairly?

evidence.quote: very few approaches exist to explicitly handle constraints in multi-objective optimization problems.
current benchmarks adopted for testing new MOEAs

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider a constrained multi-objective optimization problem (CMOP) of the form

  minimize  F(x) = (f_1(x), f_2(x), ..., f_m(x))
  subject to  g_i(x) ≤ 0,  i = 1, ..., p,
              h_j(x) = 0,  j = 1, ..., q,
              x ∈ Ω ⊆ R^n,

where m ≥ 2. A point x is feasible if all constraints are satisfied; the constrained Pareto-optimal set consists of feasible non-dominated points under the usual Pareto-dominance order on R^m.

Most multi-objective evolutionary algorithms (MOEAs) treat constraints only implicitly, by modifying the Pareto dominance relation (for example via constrained-dominance rules that prefer feasible solutions or solutions with smaller constraint violation). Address the following two-part research problem:

(a) Design constraint-handling mechanisms for MOEAs that explicitly use problem-specific constraint information (rather than merely altering the dominance relation), so that the resulting algorithm provably or empirically improves convergence to, and coverage of, the constrained Pareto front on CMOPs whose feasible region is small, disconnected, or located near the unconstrained Pareto front. Specify the mechanism, prove or experimentally demonstrate that it strictly outperforms standard constrained-dominance based MOEAs, and characterize the class of CMOPs for which the improvement holds.

(b) Construct a benchmark suite of constrained multi-objective test problems whose properties (size and topology of the feasible region, location of the constrained Pareto front relative to the unconstrained one, type and number of active constraints, scalability in m and n) are precisely controllable and representative of real-world CMOPs, together with a fair evaluation protocol (performance indicators, statistical tests, and reference sets) that allows unbiased comparison of constraint-handling techniques in MOEAs.
artifact.status_search_result: Recent surveys and papers from 2024 confirm that explicit constraint handling in multi-objective evolutionary algorithms remains an active research area. While many constraint-handling techniques (penalty functions, ε-constraint, feasibility rules, multitasking, deep-reinforcement-learning-assisted operator selection) and several benchmark suites (C-DTLZ, CTPs, MW, real-world 50-problem suite) have been proposed, no single approach or benchmark is accepted as definitive, and the design of fair evaluation protocols is still being debated. The problem is therefore broadly open.

status_evidence.title: Evolutionary constrained multi-objective optimization: a review
status_evidence.snippet: Systematically introduces six categories of constrained multi-objective evolutionary algorithms and discusses benchmark test problem sets.
status_evidence.claim: Constraint handling in MOEAs is still under active development with many competing techniques and benchmarks.

status_evidence.title: A Benchmark-Suite of real-World constrained multi-objective optimization problems
status_evidence.snippet: A benchmark suite of 50 real-world constrained multi-objective optimization problems with baseline results.
status_evidence.claim: New real-world CMOP benchmark suites continue to be proposed, indicating no consensus benchmark exists.

status_evidence.title: Adaptive constraint handling technique selection for constrained multi-objective optimization
status_evidence.snippet: Proposes adaptive selection among constraint-handling techniques for CMOPs.
status_evidence.claim: Choice of constraint-handling technique remains problem-dependent and open.
